speaker: Unknown
en: Where the fuck is all the automation?
zh: 到底他妈的自动化都在哪儿?

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is so unbelievably smart, and yet it's so useless at all other stuff.
zh: AI 聪明得难以置信,可在其他所有事情上又如此没用。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't matter how much AI coding agents you use, the software actually isn't getting better.
zh: 不管你用多少 AI 编码智能体,软件实际上并没有变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you're riding it faster.
zh: 也许你做得更快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's arguably getting worse.
zh: 可以说反而变得更糟了。

speaker: Unknown
en: OpenAI has been trying to automate customer service since 2020.
zh: OpenAI 从 2020 年就一直在尝试自动化客服。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I want instead is smart software.
zh: 我真正想要的是智能软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to expand what software itself can do such that things that should be automatable can then be automatable.
zh: 我想扩展软件本身能做的事,让那些本该可自动化的东西真正变得可自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: My favorite thing that you guys say is we build prod, not God.
zh: 我最喜欢你们说的一句话是:我们构建的是产品,不是上帝(God)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if we had any other kind of like big lab leader, even if they had joy, they would cover it up.
zh: 因为如果我们换任何一个别的大实验室领导者,即使他们心怀喜悦(joy),也会把它掩盖起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then your view is so different.
zh: 而你的看法却如此不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're like, no, we're going to create a way better world.
zh: 你说的是,不,我们要创造一个美好得多的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: For nuanced reasons, I don't think we are on the path of RSI.
zh: 出于一些微妙的原因,我认为我们并不在 RSI(递归自我改进)的道路上。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the Saspocalypse story… AI can write software, but what if the bigger opportunity is putting intelligence inside the software itself?
zh: 在 Saspocalypse(萨斯末日)的故事里……AI 能写软件,但更大的机会会不会是把智能放进软件本身?

speaker: Unknown
en: In this episode, Ben Horowitz and Martin Casado sit down with TypeSafe AI founder Diogo Almeida to talk about JEV and a different vision for how AI changes computing.
zh: 在这一集中,Ben Horowitz 和 Martin Casado 与 TypeSafe AI 创始人 Diogo Almeida 一起聊 JEV,以及 AI 如何改变计算的另一种愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: Diogo argues that coding agents make it faster to produce the same kind of software we already have.
zh: Diogo 认为,编码智能体让我们能更快地生产出我们已有的同类软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: JEV is aimed at expanding what software itself can do, giving developers a new primitive for turning natural language intent into decisions that programs can actually use.
zh: JEV 的目标是扩展软件本身能做的事,为开发者提供一个新原语,把自然语言意图转化为程序真正能使用的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: They get into why reliability matters more than impressive demos, what a new era of probabilistic programming could look like, and why AI might make existing software dramatically more useful rather than simply replacing it.
zh: 他们谈到为什么可靠性比令人惊艳的演示更重要、概率式编程的新时代可能是什么样子,以及为什么 AI 可能会让现有软件变得极其更有用,而不是简单地取代它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And beneath all of this is the question that drove Diogo to build TypeSafe in the first place.
zh: 而在这一切之下,是当初驱使 Diogo 创建 TypeSafe 的那个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: If AI is already this smart, where is all the automation?
zh: 如果 AI 已经这么聪明,那所有的自动化都到哪儿去了?

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, we have the founder and leader of TypeSafe, Diogo, with us, who is a bit of a hero to both Martine and me.
zh: 今天和我们在一起的是 TypeSafe 的创始人与领导者 Diogo,他可以说是我和 Martine 两个人的英雄。

speaker: Unknown
en: He is not only building like a really interesting product, but creating what we think is a very important movement.
zh: 他不仅在打造一个非常有趣的产品,还在掀起一场我们认为非常重要的运动。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're super excited about today.
zh: 所以我们对今天超级兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, thanks for coming.
zh: 好吧,感谢你前来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you can give us a brief on what is JEV, what is TypeSafe, why is it important?
zh: 也许你可以简单讲讲:什么是 JEV,什么是 TypeSafe,为什么它重要?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is this a curse friendly or not?
zh: 这个对文科生友好吗,还是不友好?

en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
zh: 好啊,好啊,好啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, okay, cool.
zh: 哦,好的,不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: What work are you talking about?
zh: 你说的是哪个工作?

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, okay, okay, cool.
zh: 好好好,不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I was actually asked for like an elevator pitch, which I tend to ramble on and I don't do well, but like I realized my favorite elevator pitch for JEV is where the fuck is all the automation?
zh: 我其实被人要求做过电梯演讲,而我往往絮絮叨叨讲不好,但我意识到我最喜欢的 JEV 电梯演讲就是:到底他妈的自动化都在哪儿?

speaker: Unknown
en: This is so unbelievably tragic, so much intelligence, AI is so unbelievably smart, and yet, not that I hate on chatbots or coding agents, I love them myself, but it's so useless at all other stuff, and it's tragic.
zh: 这真是难以置信的悲剧,这么多智能,AI 聪明得难以置信,可并不是说我讨厌聊天机器人或编码智能体,我自己就很喜欢它们,但它在其他所有事情上都如此没用,这很悲剧。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's tragic that we have so much diamond in the rough, but not polished for work.
zh: 我们手握这么多未经雕琢的钻石,却没打磨好拿来干活,这很悲剧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But TypeSafe is making AI for software.
zh: 而 TypeSafe 是在为软件做 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we want to make AI powerful, not just for humans in the loop, but to actually build real software.
zh: 你知道,我们想让 AI 不仅对人在环中的场景强大,而是真正用来构建真正的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Jiv to us is our first model in this whole space to make it way, way better to like make automation.
zh: 而 Jev 对我们来说,是我们在这一整个领域里的第一个模型,用来让自动化这件事好上好几个数量级。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 嗯。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's been interesting because it's kind of caught fire in software world.
zh: 所以这很有意思,因为它在软件圈有点火了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the things that made us go, what the hell's going on here is like...
zh: 所以有一件事让我们觉得,这到底是怎么回事,就是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Every developer we know is calling us and going, oh, this is frickin' awesome.

speaker: Unknown
en: It's great.

en: It's fast.

en: It's great.
zh: 很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything's better.
zh: 一切都更好了。

en: Then how does that, because everybody thinks of, well, we've got Claude Code, we've got Codex, don't we already have that?
zh: 那这就引出一个问题,因为大家都会想,我们已经有 Claude Code 了,有 Codex 了,这不就是已经有了吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what's the difference?
zh: 区别在哪儿?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then how does that lead to real automation?
zh: 而这又如何引向真正的自动化?

speaker: Unknown
en: Ooh, I wish I had some slopped visuals because I have a favorite slopped visual for this.
zh: 哦,我真希望我有一些 slop(劣质 AI 风)的视觉图,因为我为此有一个最喜欢的 slop 视觉图。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: What I want instead is smart software.
zh: 而我想要的其实是智能软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like instead of automating software engineering, I want to expand what software itself can do such that things that should be automatable can then be automatable.

speaker: Unknown
en: And like in a more flowery language, I want to express things like intent.

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so freaking cool and I want to just make that more.
zh: 这太他妈酷了，我只想把这件事做得更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Interesting.

en: So one way to think about it is

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead of kind of a tool that somewhat replaces a software engineer with a faster, maybe not even as good software engineer, what you're saying is, no, no, no, we're going to super empower the software engineers we have to write way, way better, more interesting things.
zh: 与其说它是一种多少替代了软件工程师的工具，用一个更快的、甚至可能没那么好的软件工程师，你说的是，不不不，我们要超级赋能现有的软件工程师，让他们写出好得多、有趣得多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah, so this is, by the way, I just think so many people miss this point, and it's such a subtle point, and it's so important to actually tease it out, which is, if you use something like Cloud Coder Codex, which is great, or Cursor, which is great, they write code.
zh: 对，对，顺便说一句，我觉得很多人都漏掉了这一点，这是一个非常微妙的点，把它真正梳理出来非常重要，那就是，如果你使用像 Cloud Coder Codex 这样的东西，它很棒，或者 Cursor,它也很棒，它们写代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that code is the same thing a human being would have write.
zh: 但那些代码和人类会写的东西是一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it's better, maybe it's worse, but it's basically still code, just like code looked 10 years ago.
zh: 也许更好，也许更差，但它基本上仍然是代码，就像 10 年前的代码一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing with JEV is, whether or not you're a Cloud Coder or a human, you have this new primitive
zh: 而 Jev 的特别之处在于，无论你是 Cloud Coder 还是一个人类，你都拥有这个新的原语

speaker: Unknown
en: This new thing that you stick in your code that actually expands the power of software.
zh: 这个你放进代码里的新东西，它真正拓展了软件的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So instead of, like, writing code, it is something that you include in your code.
zh: 所以，它不是，比如说，写代码，而是你把它包含在你的代码里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which, by the way, is interesting because it's this very powerful primitive, which would be great if you explain, but it's also a little bit different than, like, how programmers think.
zh: 顺便说一句，这很有意思，因为这是一个非常强大的原语，如果你能解释一下就太好了，但它也和程序员的思维方式有点不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, like, it has this notion of probabilities or maybe… So an intelligent layer inside the software.
zh: 比如说，它有概率或者可能……这样的概念，所以是软件内部的一个智能层。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, think of like a library that you can use natural language to describe what you want and you give it kind of a state machine and then it will choose what to do with some confidence levels, which we kind of haven't really had before.
zh: 是的，把它想成一个库，你可以用自然语言描述你想要什么，然后你给它一个状态机，接着它会以一定的置信度选择要做什么，这是我们以前其实没有过的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ooh, there's a lot of tricks there.
zh: 哦，这里面有很多技巧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will jump into one thing first, which is I love the first thing you said in the direction of where the fuck is all the automation.
zh: 我会先跳进一件事，那就是我喜欢你最开始说的那个方向，他妈的自动化都在哪儿。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love software so much.
zh: 我太爱软件了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wish I could be writing it all day.
zh: 我真希望能整天写代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: Would not recommend being a CEO to people, but whatever.
zh: 我不推荐别人当 CEO,不过无所谓了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also it's wild that AI is so cool and software has been unchanged in 10 years.
zh: 而且很离谱的是，AI 这么酷，而软件这 10 年却毫无变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, like that to me, like no one can square this together.
zh: 你知道，对我来说，这一点没人能把这两者调和起来。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我们最多能做到的，就是有时在旁边加个小聊天机器人，它可以执行某些操作，但不是所有操作，因为有些操作并不可靠。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I just want to give that tiny aside.
zh: 所以我只是想先插这么一句小话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love the point.
zh: 我很喜欢这个观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to jump back to the point about this is a little bit of a different way to think about it.
zh: 我要跳回这个观点，这是一种不太一样的思考方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, I think that machine native doesn't exactly match bits perfectly.
zh: 是的，我认为 machine native 并不能和 bits 完美匹配。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's actually the art form that we are trying to do.
zh: 而这其实就是我们试图做的艺术。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in the middle.

en: But things like probabilities are not exactly novel.
zh: 但像概率这样的东西并不算特别新颖。

en: Or do you think like this is like the point in the design space, which is language in, kind of state machine out, which is going to solidify as the general purpose thing for programmers?
